messages.subject: geom_smooth with arrow?
parts:
hi

starting with

xval<-1:100
yval<-rnorm(100)
qplot(xval,yval)+xlim(-10,100)+geom_smooth(method="lm")

now all i need is an arrowhead or a red dot or something where the
regression line hits x=-10. i saw that geom_path has arrowheads and
dots, but i can't make a connection.

any help would be greatly appreciated!
-neal

messages.author: 4e69b94a09c8cf3b
messages.subject: Re: geom_smooth with arrow?
parts:
Not sure I understand your example. The regression line won't hit
x=-10. Are you trying to estimate yval at x=-10? Do you need an lm to
predict that yval from the data?

You can put a vertical line at x=-10.

qplot(xval,yval)+xlim(-10,100)+geom_smooth(method="lm")+geom_vline(x=-10, color="red")

dev.new()
yval=c(predict(lm(yval~xval),data.frame(xval=-10,yval=NA))[[1]],yval)
xval=c(-10,xval)
qplot(xval,yval)+xlim(-10,100)+geom_smooth(method="lm")+geom_vline(x=-10, color="red")


If you have your data in a data frame, you can add a variable to
differentiate observed from predicted and use the difference to color
the points by the difference factor.

messages.author: 20a7dc1f521322f3
messages.subject: Re: geom_smooth with arrow?
parts: sorry in my example i meant

qplot(xval,yval)+xlim(-10,100)+geom_smooth(method="lm",fullrange=T)

with fullrange=T

now that i see your solution, it's almost exactly what i
want, except i want that predicted point red or some
arrowhead there.

so following your suggestion, i did

fullx<-c(-10,1:100)
fully<-c(predict(lm(yval~xval),data.frame(xval=-10,yval=NA))
[[1]],yval)
fullp<-c(TRUE,rep(FALSE,100))
thedf<-data.frame(thex=fullx,they=fully,thep=fullp)
ggplot(thedf,aes(x=thex,y=they,color=thep))+geom_point()
+geom_smooth(method=lm,fullrange=T)

which is, again, almost what i want, except now i think the standard
error that geom_smooth is drawing seems to be smaller since
it's including the predicted point in the regression (not
changing the line itself though i think).

neal

messages.author: 4e69b94a09c8cf3b
messages.subject: Re: geom_smooth with arrow?
parts:
I don't think the line would change with predictions from a linear
model. You can add a group aesthetic if you are impacting the standard
error. The standard error of the estimated group should be zero for
your model.
